The overall mission will come to a conclusion tomorrow, April 10th when Astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, & Jeremy Hansen flying in the Orion spacecraft (“Integrity”) re-enter Earth’s atmosphere & then splashes down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, CA around ~8:07 PM EDT (~5:07 PM PDT) So, what can we expect to see? Re-entry for the Orion spacecraft is a critical moment in the mission as it will be traveling far faster than any spacecraft with humans on board other than those during the Apollo era because of the speeds involved with lunar-return trajectories. Entry interface (typically defined at ~400,000 feet / ~122 km altitude) is where atmospheric effects become significant) At that point, the Orion capsule will be at ~24,000 to ~25,000 mph (~38,600 to ~40,200 km/h or ~11 km/s) which is comparable to or slightly below Apollo-era lunar returns.
